identity.name: Brown HT
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic azo dye (bis-azo sulfonated food colour)

function.mechanism: The azo chromophore absorbs visible light and imparts brown coloration to foods.

adi.basis: EFSA re-evaluation maintained ADI; later refined exposure assessment identified high-percentile exceedance in some population groups under some scenarios.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA maintained ADI of 1.5 mg/kg bw/day for Brown HT (E155); refined exposure work reported scenario-dependent ADI exceedance mainly in high consumers, especially younger age groups.

fda.cfr_citation: No Brown HT listing in retrieved Title 21 eCFR API searches; related but different listing: 21 CFR 74.2151 (D&C Brown No. 1)

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry for BROWN HT reports ADI range 0-1.5 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: A 2024 rat study reported mammary tumour-related findings after Brown HT exposure, suggesting a potential carcinogenic signal in that model.

EFSA exposure scenarios identified potential ADI exceedance at the 95th percentile in some age groups, indicating a population-level exposure management concern rather than definitive hazard confirmation.

no_concern_confirmed: Historical long-term and multigeneration animal studies indexed in PubMed did not report clear treatment-related carcinogenic or reproductive toxicity in their summaries.
JECFA and EFSA both retain numeric ADIs for Brown HT rather than withdrawing authorization in the retrieved records.

populations: High consumers of foods containing Brown HT
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined exposure assessment reported 95th percentile exceedance in some scenarios and age groups (except elderly in that analysis), while reported-use scenarios were below ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Brown HT remains authorized with established ADIs, but EFSA high-percentile exposure caveats and newer animal-signal literature support a cautious middle-tier classification rather than low concern.
key_factors: EFSA and JECFA ADIs are established
EFSA exposure scenarios indicate possible ADI exceedance in some groups
Recent animal study raises potential mammary tumour concern
No direct IARC classification found in current IARC classification dataset
